content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"Program element 0603160BR, \"Counter Weapons of Mass Destruction Advanced Technology Development,\" is run by the Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) and funded through the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Defense-Wide account.","citation":{"fact_id":"8af4a1583e5f79a0"}},{"text":"The program develops advanced technologies and weapon concepts and validates their applicability to countering weapons of mass destruction (CWMD), spanning defeat technologies, rapid capability delivery, counter-emergent threat technologies, counterforce technologies, and target assessment technologies.","citation":{"fact_id":"a3feebd1055638e4"}},{"text":"One line of research, in support of the U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), pursues counter-proliferation work to defeat WMD development and acquisition pathways as well as concepts to prevent violent extremist organizations and rogue nation states from developing, acquiring, or using WMD.","citation":{"fact_id":"a3feebd1055638e4"}},{"text":"Project RD, Nuclear Technologies and Capabilities Development, develops, integrates, and transitions radiation detection technologies and systems, along with tools and techniques using non-radiation-based signatures, to help warfighters rapidly detect, localize, characterize, and interdict nuclear and radiological threats.","citation":{"fact_id":"ffaa0d790bcb3cfd"}},{"text":"Project RA, CWMD Cross-Cutting Technical and Information Sciences, develops modeling and simulation capabilities and provides technical reachback support across the full CWMD mission space for the United States and its allies.","citation":{"fact_id":"b817c23eafdedaa2"}},{"text":"Project RR, CWMD Test and Evaluation, provides a national test capability for simulated WMD facilities and processes, leveraging 50 years of expertise in investigating weapons effects and target response, including tests against above-ground, cut-and-cover, and deep underground tunnel facilities.","citation":{"fact_id":"c09af177086f1f15"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"For fiscal year 2024, the program recorded actual spending of about $390.6 million (listed as $390,581 thousand).","citation":{"fact_id":"8af4a1583e5f79a0"}},{"text":"For fiscal year 2025 the program was enacted at about $410.1 million (listed as $410,112 thousand).","citation":{"fact_id":"e9edae2334960c73"}},{"text":"The fiscal year 2026 request drops to about $393.5 million (listed as $393,469 thousand).","citation":{"fact_id":"3be6230338c2df42"}},{"text":"That represents a decrease of about $16.6 million, or roughly 4 percent, from the FY2025 total to the FY2026 request.","citation":{"fact_id":"a6923935a11b50e5"}},{"text":"Within the program, the CWMD Technologies and Capabilities Development project (RG) is the largest budget-year effort, requested at about $233.7 million for the coming budget year.","citation":{"fact_id":"8086c8a8e1329e89"}},{"text":"The Nuclear Technologies and Capabilities Development project (RD) is requested at about $84.2 million for the coming budget year.","citation":{"fact_id":"950aae62b65a9b19"}},{"text":"The CWMD Cross-Cutting Technical and Information Sciences project (RA) is requested at about $63.6 million for the coming budget year.","citation":{"fact_id":"be9bbe6acb36a511"}},{"text":"The CWMD Test and Evaluation project (RR) is the smallest, requested at about $12.1 million for the coming budget year.","citation":{"fact_id":"bc129c2cba6783b8"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"The program is managed by the Defense Threat Reduction Agency
